name: Metformin
summary: The foundational type 2 diabetes drug that lowers hepatic glucose output and usually avoids hypoglycemia on its own.
good: Type 2 diabetes when a low-cost, high-value foundation drug is needed.
bad: Significant renal dysfunction or persistent GI intolerance without dose strategy adjustment.
clinicalPearls: It is weight-neutral to mildly weight-lowering and usually low risk for hypoglycemia.
mechanism: Reduces hepatic gluconeogenesis and improves insulin sensitivity, with additional gut-mediated metabolic effects.
indications: First-line type 2 diabetes, insulin resistance, and polycystic-ovary-syndrome-related metabolic support in some settings.
interactionNotes: Contrast studies, renal decline, and other lactic-acidosis risk situations warrant review.

warnings: GI upset, B12 reduction, and kidney-function limits are the core issues.
